title.rendered: Another Advocate, With You Forever: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: Another Advocate. That is what Jesus promised the Father would give. Not a substitute. Another of the same kind, with you forever. The promise still stands.

content.rendered:
Another Advocate. That is what Jesus promised the Father would give. Not a substitute. Another of the same kind, with you forever. Pentecost does not begin with the fire of Acts 2. It begins with this promise in John 14. And the promise still stands.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, May 18, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“And I will ask the Father, and he will give you another advocate to help you and be with you forever—the Spirit of truth.”
John 14:16–17 (NIV)

Today’s Message

Yesterday we looked at Joel, eight hundred years before Pentecost, glimpsing the day God would pour out His Spirit on all flesh. Today we move closer in time and closer to the upper room. Jesus is sitting with the disciples on the night before He goes to the cross. He has just told them He is leaving. The room is heavy with that announcement. And then He speaks a promise that begins to lift it.

I will ask the Father. The Father will give you another advocate. He will be with you forever.

The Greek word translated “another” is allos—another of the same kind. Not a different sort of being. Not a downgrade. Not a lesser version. The Helper coming would be of the very same nature as the One who was leaving. The Spirit who would arrive at Pentecost would not be less than Jesus. He would be God Himself, present in His people in a new way.

Then notice the second word: advocate. The Greek is parakletos—one called alongside. He stands with you, speaks for you, strengthens you, comforts you. He is not someone you have to summon by performance. He is not someone you have to earn by intensity. The Father gave Him to you because of what Jesus did. He is not a reward for the strong. He is a gift to the believing.

And then the last word that should land on you today: forever. In the Old Testament, the Spirit came on people for a season and a task. Saul. Samson. Bezalel. The Spirit would come and the Spirit would leave. But Jesus is promising something new here. The advocate is not a temporary visitor. He is a permanent resident. With you forever.

If you belong to Christ today, this promise is your inheritance. The Spirit of God is in you. Not as a guest who might leave. Not as a measure parcelled out based on your last week of obedience. He is with you forever, because the work of Jesus is finished and the gift of the Father has been given. Let that settle into your heart as this Pentecost week begins.

Prayer

Father, thank You for the gift of Your Spirit. He is not a reward I have earned. He is a gift You have given because of what Jesus has done. I receive Him today as my Advocate, my Comforter, the One called alongside. Let me walk through this week aware that I am not alone, never alone, and forever held. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

The Father has given me another Advocate. The Holy Spirit is in me, with me, and for me, not because I am strong but because Jesus is finished. I am never alone. The Advocate is with me forever. That is the promise of Pentecost. That is my inheritance in Christ.
